newsitem.title: USA: Stocks end mixed as technology issues rise.
newsitem.headline: Stocks end mixed as technology issues rise.

text.p: Stocks closed on a mixed note Thursday as fresh economic data further stoked inflation fears in the bond market, driving down blue chips while the high-technology sector again stole the show and drew avid buying.

The Dow Jones industrial average closed 9.62 points lower at 5,867.74. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,242 to 1,102 on active volume of 395 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq index was up 6.38 points at 1,212.09, nearing its record close of 1,249.15 set on June 5.
"It's a day where techs are up and the rest of the market is languishing," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.
"A lot of the big-cap techs that have been strong are staying strong and the former high-flyers that were killed (in the July market correction) are coming back," he said.
The Nasdaq index, which is studded with high technology stocks, has surged 6 percent since the start of September, while the Dow Jones index has risen only 4 percent during the same period.

Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker, said some of the key technology stocks were benefitting from "window-dressing," or buying by portfolio managers to make their accounts look stronger at the end of the third quarter.

Among technology stocks, Intel rose 1-3/8 to 97 after jumping to a 52-week high of 97-1/2 early in the day. The stock has climbed 19 percent so far this month, with more buying sparked after Intel on Monday forecast that it will post stronger-than-expected third-quarter revenues.
Software giant Microsoft rose 1-1/4 to 137-3/4, Micron rose 1-7/8 to 27-3/8, Hewlett-Packard rose 1/4 to 48-3/8 while International Business Machines lost 1 to 123-1/2 after its recent rally.

Interest-rate sensitive blue chip stocks, however, were hounded anew by worries that strong economic growth may provoke the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at next Tuesday's policy-setting meeting to ward off inflation.

Strong housing starts, lower-than-expected weekly jobless claims and a jump in the Philadelphia Federal Reserve's regional prices index for September lent more credence to expectations that the Fed may boost interest rates.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was off 12/32 raising its yield to 7.05 percent from 7.03 percent at Wednesday's close.
Among individual shares, Ethan Allen surged 3-1/8 to 30-5/8 after forecasting that its quarterly results would exceed Wall Street's expectations.
Three initial public offerings were among the Nasdaq's best performers.

Cymer Corp., a maker of excimer lasers for deep ultraviolet photolithography systems used in the production of the very small images in advanced semiconductor chips, soared 43 percent or 4-1/8 to 13-5/8.
Rental Services Corp., which rents out pumps, generators, forklifts and other industrial equipment, rose 5-3/4 points to 21-3/4, or 36 percent on its first day of trading.
Another IPO, RMH Teleservices, rose 2-1/2 to 15. RMH provides outbound teleservices for insurance and financial services companies.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 1.53 to 683.00. The American Stock Exchange index was off 1.21 to 565.44.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.50 to 363.94. The average share was up 5 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,701.737 up 14.581 or 0.22 percent.
